solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Smiles, having old pennies hidden inside jars

indicators.note: the pennies are tucked within the word for smiles, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: smiles broadly means grins
D was the abbreviation for the old British penny (from Latin denarius)

explanation.surface: Someone grinning about the pre-decimal coins stashed away in some jam jars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jars' looks like a plural noun for containers, but it is a verb: grates or rasps.
explanation.definitionFit: To jar is to grate harshly, as gears do when they rasp against each other.

clue.text: It's good joining group of stars with my entertainment award

parts.note: the Ram is the constellation Aries

explanation.surface: A celebrity collecting an entertainment prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'group of stars' suggests celebrities, but it is a constellation, Aries the Ram.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual American music industry prize, named after the gramophone.

clue.text: Individuals entering one Asian country from another

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes into the other

parts.note: another Asian country here is India
individuals are single ones

explanation.surface: Migrants travelling from one Asian nation to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one Asian country' is the definition; 'another' Asian country is the container INDIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The south-east Asian archipelago nation whose capital is Jakarta.

clue.text: Man's beginning to entertain old city as a stage performer

parts.note: a man's, as in Dan's

indicators.note: the beginning of entertain is its first letter

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A man starts entertaining an ancient city as an actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man's' must be read as one man named, DAN'S, giving DANS.
explanation.definitionFit: A male ballet dancer, the French term used on the ballet stage.

clue.text: Disease in record supplied by one new medic

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of medic are made over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A doctor's notes recording an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal, reshuffling the doctor's title; 'supplied by' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An outbreak of illness spreading widely through a population is this kind of disease.

clue.text: Indicating an error with the way the psalm is being sung?

definitions.text: an error with the way the psalm is being sung?
definitions.meaning: pointing is the marking of psalm text for chanting; if it is wrong, the pointing is out

explanation.surface: A choirmaster noting a mistake in the chanting.
explanation.walkthrough: Pointing is the marks in a psalter showing how words fit the chant.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing attention to something, as one does with an outstretched finger.

clue.text: Lecture lad with mice being mistreated

indicators.note: being mistreated suggests letters roughly handled and put in disorder

explanation.surface: Scolding a boy for being cruel to rodents.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak rhetorically and forcefully, as a lecturer or orator does.

clue.text: Opening about four weeks — there's been a change of heart

indicators.text: there's been a change of heart
indicators.note: the central letter of the word is replaced by another

parts.note: a month is roughly four weeks

explanation.surface: An opening a month ago, with a change of mind since.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle N of MONTH is changed to U.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrance or aperture, as of a river or cave.

clue.text: Trace any random curve

indicators.note: random says the letters are put in any order

explanation.surface: Draw a curve, any curve at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The curve a hanging chain or cable makes between two supports.

clue.text: Extremely keen to have e.g. paintings displayed around studio?

indicators.note: the paintings are set out around the studio, so that word encloses the other

parts.note: paintings are examples of art
a den is a private room or study where one works

explanation.surface: An artist so enthusiastic they hang their pictures all round the workroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Passionate, fervent enthusiasm is the sense here; the word comes from Latin for burning.

clue.text: Take no notice of sales ploy?

definitions.meaning: to disregard or dismiss something as unimportant
a price reduction used by shops to draw in buyers

explanation.surface: Ignore the shop's marketing gimmick.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to disregard; the noun is a reduction in price offered to tempt shoppers.

clue.text: Fellow needing to produce vegetable

parts.note: a fellow is a man
to produce or bring out something is to get it out

explanation.surface: A man who has to grow some greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' looks like a noun for vegetables, but it is a verb meaning bring out.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-podded pea eaten whole, pod and all, is a garden vegetable; the French name means eat-all.

clue.text: Authoritarian maiden perhaps leading course

indicators.note: leading puts the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: a maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored
a course or direction is a bearing

explanation.surface: A girl who leads the class is bossy.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden is a cricket over (six balls) from which no runs come.
explanation.definitionFit: Domineering and bossy, imposing one's will on others.

clue.text: Looking ill in rash endeavour

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words rash endeavour

explanation.surface: Someone pale and unwell after attempting something reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey and pale in the face, as someone ill or shocked looks, the colour of cinders.

clue.text: Trojan 'gems' are disciplined — one bawls at the soldiers!

indicators.note: disciplined suggests letters drilled and put into new order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Trojan troops called 'gems' are punished by the officer who shouts at them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disciplined' reorders TROJAN GEMS ARE; the exclamation mark points to the drill-square shouter.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior non-commissioned officer famous for barking orders on the parade ground.

clue.text: Islanders preserve excellent metal containers

parts.note: jam is a fruit preserve
A1 means first-rate, written AI
cans are metal containers

explanation.surface: Islanders preserve fruit in fine tins.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is written with the letter I for the figure 1.
explanation.definitionFit: People from the Caribbean island nation whose capital is Kingston.

clue.text: Opinionated beast — dull and in charge

parts.note: a dog is a beast or animal
matt or mat means dull, not shiny

explanation.surface: A slow animal that bosses others about.
explanation.definitionFit: Asserting views as certain truths, dismissive of other opinions.

clue.text: You want to see flower — so go on rambles possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of so go on rambles might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: To see a particular bloom you must go on country walks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambles' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'possibly' does the rearranging. 'You want to see' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: The fragrant white bloom of the citrus tree, traditionally worn by brides.

clue.text: What may be handed over by barmaids (good girls)

definitions.text: What may be handed over by barmaids

parts.note: lasses are girls

explanation.surface: Barmaids, nice girls, serving customers.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinking vessels that bar staff pass across the counter to customers.

clue.text: Dawn is nurse misbehaving

indicators.note: misbehaving says the letters behave badly and fall out of order

explanation.surface: A nurse called Dawn behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dawn' looks like the nurse's name, but it is daybreak.
explanation.definitionFit: The first light of morning, daybreak.

clue.text: One with terrible anger prepared to move?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: terrible suggests the letters of anger are in a dreadful state, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone in a fearful rage is ready to go.
explanation.definitionFit: A car with a gear engaged is ready to drive off, so it is set to go.

clue.text: Obsession in Philippines capital putting learner off

indicators.note: putting, with off, says a letter is put off, that is removed from the city name
putting the learner off means removing that letter from the city name

parts.note: Manila is the capital of the Philippines
L is the learner plate on British cars

explanation.surface: A craze in Manila that has driving pupils kept off the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A craze or excessive enthusiasm, an all-consuming fixation.

clue.text: English lecturer's first to go after recently instituted post

indicators.note: after says the English piece and lecturer's letter come after the first piece

parts.note: recently instituted means new

indicators.note: first takes the initial letter of lecturer's

explanation.surface: An English lecturer leaves for a newly created job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' looks like a job but is a pillar at the end of a staircase banister.
explanation.definitionFit: The upright pillar at the top or bottom of a stair that supports the handrail.

clue.text: Word from 14 offered with care

definitions.meaning: the drill command shouted by the parade-ground officer of 14 across

explanation.surface: The officer's command, given with concern.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the parade-ground order to stand straight and the general sense of heedfulness or notice.

clue.text: Community has hospital — dump seen on the outside

indicators.note: the dump is seen around the outside of the other pieces, so it encloses them

parts.note: a tip is a rubbish dump
has means owns

explanation.surface: A town that has a hospital with a rubbish dump next to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' is the British word for a rubbish dump.
explanation.definitionFit: A small town or settlement; in South Africa, an urban area set aside under apartheid.

clue.text: End component of Cambridge college lacking in its Oxford counterpart

definitions.meaning: the closing part of a show or piece of music

definitions.text: component of Cambridge college lacking in its Oxford counterpart
definitions.meaning: Magdalene at Cambridge ends in a letter that Magdalen at Oxford lacks: the last letter E

explanation.surface: The difference between two Oxbridge colleges comes at the very end.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge has Magdalene College, Oxford has Magdalen College; read the answer as two words, FINAL E.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing number or movement of a performance is its concluding part.

clue.text: Transmission from broadcaster — in panic all's ignored

indicators.note: in tells us the letters lie inside the words panic all's ignored

explanation.surface: During a crisis everyone's message goes unheeded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' looks like a deletion signal, but it is part of the run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The identifying letters and numbers a radio station or operator sends out on air.

clue.text: In first two bits of translation language is more succinct

indicators.note: In here means the language sits inside the opening letters
the first two letters of the word translation are taken

parts.note: Erse is Irish Gaelic

explanation.surface: Translating the opening of a text into another tongue makes it shorter.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefer and more curt; a comparative adjective, matching more succinct.
